The Katsina State Government has constituted a nine-member investigative committee to probe the alleged sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Farouk Umar, following public concerns generated by the allegation. The committee, approved by Governor Dikko Radda, is expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the allegation and determine the extent of the monarch’s culpability. The development was announced in a statement by the state Commissioner for Information and Culture, Dr Bala Zango, made available to newsmen on Thursday in Katsina. According to the statement, the committee is chaired by retired Justice Amiru Sanusi, while the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Fadila Dikko, will serve as secretary. Other members include the Special Adviser on Emirate Affairs, Usman Abba; retired Justice Sadiq A. Mahuta; the Commissioner for Religious Affairs, Isah Dabai; Lawal Aliyu Daura; Professor Halima Kabir of the Department of Languages and Cultures, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria; Zango; and the Belgium Kingdom’s Economic Diplomacy Adviser, Khadija Abdulkadir. The committee’s terms of reference include investigating the allegation, inviting all persons connected with the matter and determining the actual purpose of the foreign tourist’s visit to the Emir’s palace. It is also expected to examine relevant documents, records and other evidence, establish the extent of the Emir’s culpability and recommend appropriate sanctions where necessary. The government further mandated the panel to recommend measures to prevent a recurrence of similar incidents. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. It added that the panel had four weeks from the date of its inauguration to complete the assignment and submit its findings to the state government. The investigation comes amid public attention surrounding the allegation against the traditional ruler, which has generated discussions about accountability, the responsibilities of traditional institutions and the handling of allegations involving public figures. In a related development, the state government appealed to members of the public to refrain from making statements or taking actions capable of prejudicing the investigation. The government urged citizens to allow the committee to carry out its assignment without undue pressure or interference. “Government also wishes to assure citizens that justice will be served based on the outcome of the investigation,” the statement added. The outcome of the investigation is expected to determine the next steps by the state government regarding the allegation and any possible disciplinary measures. Katsina orders Emirs to obtain clearance before hosting foreigners Allow traditional rulers to receive opposition politicians, Saraki tells Abdulrazaq Daura: Katsina orders emirs to seek clearance before receiving foreign guests The controversy followed an allegation by a Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, who accused the Emir of Daura of sexually assaulting her during a visit to his palace on November 14, 2026. Czee, who was born in the Czech Republic, made the allegation in a series of Instagram posts after completing a 30-day tour of Nigeria. She said she waited until she had left the country before speaking publicly about the incident. Recounting her experience, the tourist alleged that the Emir held her hand, hugged and kissed her on the cheek before touching her breasts without her consent. She said she repeatedly told him not to touch her. She also claimed to have recorded part of the encounter using Meta smart glasses, with footage of the meeting subsequently circulating on social media. The allegation attracted widespread reactions, prompting Amnesty International Nigeria to call on the Katsina State Government and the police to conduct a transparent and independent investigation. The human rights organisation described the allegation as disturbing and said the authorities should demonstrate that nobody was above the law. The Daura Emirate Council subsequently said it was reviewing the viral footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated or artificially generated. An unnamed source in the Emir’s palace, however, denied the allegation, insisting that nothing of the sort happened during the tourist’s visit. The source said Czee visited the palace but questioned her account of the encounter. The Emir had not personally responded to the allegation in PUNCH’s earlier reports. Following the controversy, the Katsina State Government announced the suspension of the Emir’s official engagements and travels pending the outcome of an investigation. Governor Dikko Radda also directed the establishment of an investigative committee to examine the allegation and recommend appropriate action. The controversy also generated concerns over the safety of the tourist after Amnesty International condemned death threats and online harassment directed at her following the publication of the video. In a further response, the Katsina State Government on November 25 directed traditional rulers across the state to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors at their palaces. The directive requires emirs to seek approval from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters under the Office of the Secretary to the State Government. The government said the directive was intended to strengthen security, improve coordination and ensure compliance with official protocols during visits by foreign nationals to emirates’ palaces. It also placed traditional rulers under a formal regulatory framework for international relations. Faith Maji
